reference.title: This / That / These / Those
reference.rule: Used to refer to situations or people mentioned before. This/These generally refer to things closer in time/space (Present), while That/Those refer to things further away (Past).
examples: I studied biology. That allowed me to work in a lab.
I am taking an English course. This will give me more opportunities.

substitution.title: Auxiliary Verbs (do/does/did)
substitution.rule: Used to avoid repeating the main verb.
examples: Peter didn't study, but I did.

substitution.title: Do so
substitution.rule: Used to replace a Verb + Object structure.
examples: Peter didn't buy a new car, but I did so.

substitution.title: So / Neither
substitution.rule: Structures 'So + aux + subject' and 'Neither + aux + subject' used for agreements.
examples: I like apples. So do I.
I don't like apples. Neither do I.

substitution.title: So / Not (after certain verbs)
substitution.rule: Used after verbs like think, suppose, expect, believe, hope, seem.
examples: Is he coming? I hope so.
Will it rain? I expect not.

substitution.title: If so / If not
substitution.rule: Used to replace complete conditional clauses.
examples: Are you free tonight? If so, let's grab dinner.

substitution.title: One / Ones
examples: I've lost my books. The ones on the table are mine.

ellipsis.title: Connectors 'And/But'
ellipsis.rule: We can omit the subject or adjective if it is the same.
examples: He opened the door and (he) walked in.

ellipsis.title: Relative Pronouns
ellipsis.rule: We can omit 'which/that' when it is the direct object of the relative clause.
examples: The car (that) I bought is very fast.

ellipsis.title: Auxiliary Verbs
ellipsis.rule: We can omit the main verb after the auxiliary.
examples: Have you finished? Yes, I have (finished).

ellipsis.title: Infinitive 'to'
ellipsis.rule: We can leave the 'to' alone when omitting the rest of the infinitive clause.
examples: I didn't like chess, but I used to (like chess).

ellipsis.title: Wh- words
ellipsis.rule: We can leave the wh-word alone.
examples: He left early, but I don't know why (he left early).

speaking.structure: Regarding [Topic A], [Comment]. THAT being said, THIS other picture...
speaking.example: Regarding the first photo, they seem busy. THAT being said, THIS other picture shows a calmer environment.

speaking.structure: I think [Opinion]. Do you? -> Yes, I DO / So DO I / Neither DO I.
speaking.example: I think we should prioritize the environment over profits. Do you? -> Yes, I DO. Actually, SO DO most young people nowadays.

speaking.structure: Will [Event] happen? / Is [Idea] true? -> I certainly hope SO / I suppose NOT.
speaking.example: Do you think artificial intelligence will replace teachers? I certainly hope NOT, but I suppose SO if we rely on it too much.

speaking.structure: I haven't/didn't [Action], but I would love TO / I used TO.
speaking.example: I haven't tried any extreme sports yet, but I'd love TO if I ever get the chance.
